positions.name: SettledDecisionRatification
positions.frame: Is this expression performing a decision already settled and binding on the organization, rather than proposing or arguing for one?
positions.why: src-1 and src-3 declare the Zypherion adoption and the migration timeline in present/future performative form ('we are adopting', 'starts next quarter'), and src-4/src-6 restate the identical content as bold-label summary entries. The conviction dimension's own mint groups exactly this set under a shared 'decision' region — a choice recorded as operational fact the organization is expected to align with rather than debate. Relational reads mark all four as authority-ranking (commitment-markers, performed-acts binding the group to a schedule/choice), and power reads them as legitimate positional authority. The prose and summary forms are two deliveries of the same settled stance, which is why they cohere as one group despite differing surface register (matter-of-fact bold-label vs plain declarative).

positions.name: QuantifiedPerformanceJustification
positions.frame: Is this expression offering quantified evidence to justify a decision, rather than performing the decision itself?
positions.why: src-2 and src-5 both state the same 15x columnar-query figure — once in prose ('It handles columnar queries 15x faster'), once in bold-label summary form ('15x improvement on columnar queries'). The conviction dimension marks both as 'claim' rather than 'decision' — unhedged comparative assertions offered as grounds, not ratifications. Relational reads frame them as market-pricing (proportional cost-benefit reasoning) and power reads them as rational-persuasion/expert, distinct from the authority-ranking/legitimate-power character of the adoption and timeline statements. This group holds the justificatory evidence apart from the decision it supports, even though both restatements sit adjacent to the decision statements in the document.
